lines: Come in, look at anything, ask anything. This week I mean that in a way I did not before.
There is a notice in the window with four names on it and a date against each one. Read it going past.
We are a Foundation. People gave us money. They are owed a great deal more than a look at it.
A Crest already. You will be going east, then, and everybody going east
should have one of our storm cards. Take two. They are free, they are always free.
Come in, look at anything, ask anything. That is the whole idea of the place.
We are a Foundation. People give us money, so people are owed a look at it.
Eleven stations, on a bicycle, and every reading I take now goes to the Press on the Friday.
They asked me whether I minded. Nobody in eleven years has asked me whether I minded anything.
Ask me about April. Go on. This time actually ask me about April.
Forty weather stations and I service eleven of them, on a bicycle.
You would not believe what it does to a person, reading rain for a living.
Ask me about April. Do not actually ask me about April.
My brother is still on the coast. He has written four pages, which he has never once done.
He did not know. Nobody on his floor knew. He read it in a paper the same as the rest of us.
He is staying. He says somebody down there ought to be a person who is only good at instruments.
My brother went to them in the spring. Better wage than the sheds,
and a coat, and they taught him to read an instrument.
He is on the coast now. He writes. He does not say very much in the letters,
but he writes, which he never once did when he worked here.
